blocks.explanation:
Use \(1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}\) to turn the integrand into \(\frac{1}{2}x\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\).
Plan: integrate by parts with \(x\) first, \(\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\) second.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x}{1 + \cos x}\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: use \(1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}\); then integration by parts with \(x\) first and \(\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\) second.

Half-angle identity
\[1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[\int \dfrac{x}{2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int x\sec^2\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx\]
Why: \(\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1\) with \(\theta = \frac{x}{2}\).

Integration by parts
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[x\cdot 2\tan\dfrac{x}{2} - \int 2\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx\right]\]
\[= x\tan\dfrac{x}{2} - \int \tan\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx\]
Why: \(\int \sec^2\frac{x}{2}\,dx = 2\tan\frac{x}{2}\) (divide by \(\frac{1}{2}\), i.e. multiply by 2).

Integrate \(\tan\frac{x}{2}\)
\[\int \tan\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx = 2\ln\left|\sec\dfrac{x}{2}\right|\]
\[= x\tan\dfrac{x}{2} - 2\ln\left|\sec\dfrac{x}{2}\right| + c\]
Why: \(\int \tan kx\,dx = \frac{1}{k}\ln|\sec kx|\) with \(k = \frac{1}{2}\).
